sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for question answering
sections.what: Brings in the schema library, the AI chat helper, the model picker, the recipe type, and the filter that keeps only admitted facts.
sections.why: Likely reason: the module needs these pieces to answer questions from saved facts.

sections.name: answerSchema, verdictSchema
sections.title: Shapes of the answer and verdict
sections.what: Defines the required form of an answer (text, basis, fact IDs) and of the second model's verdict (supported yes or no, and a reason). Replies that do not match are treated as errors.
sections.why: Likely reason: the code only trusts model output after checking its shape.
sections.watch_out: Answer text is capped at 10,000 characters and fact IDs at 20, so longer model output fails as an error rather than being cut short.

sections.name: answerPresentationQuestion
sections.title: Answer a question from admitted facts
sections.what: Selects up to 20 relevant admitted facts, asks a model for an answer, and asks a second model to check it. If the check fails or the answer has no basis, returns exact matching quotes instead. Returns the text and the IDs of the facts used.
sections.why: Likely reason: the design refuses unsupported claims, so the fallback shows verified quotes instead.
sections.watch_out: Facts are picked by simple keyword matches, so a differently worded question can miss relevant facts, and any model or parse failure throws instead of returning a fallback.

summary: Answers a question about one saved lessons run using only admitted facts, then checks the answer with a second model before showing it.
purpose: Let a reader ask questions of a saved presentation and get answers that point back to exact source statements.
why: The code states the intent that answers may use only admitted claims, with no new research or causal conclusions. The two-pass design is likely meant to catch unsupported answers.
how: First, keep only admitted facts. Second, narrow to any project named in the question. Third, rank facts by keyword matches with the question. Fourth, select up to 20 facts within a size limit. Fifth, ask a model for a JSON answer with cited fact IDs. Sixth, reject answers with no valid basis or unknown IDs. Seventh, ask a second model to verify the answer against the same facts. Eighth, return the answer with a coverage note, or fall back to matching quotes.
inputs: A saved recipe object (projects, facts, pillars and methodology) and the user's question text.
outputs: An object with text and a list of fact IDs. The text is either a checked answer, a set of exact quotes with a note that the answer was not validated, or a fixed message when no admitted facts exist.
risks: Model replies are treated as untrusted and must pass shape and reference checks. A wrong verdict from the second model could let an unsupported answer through or reject a good one. Fact selection uses simple keyword matches, so differently worded questions can miss facts. Model calls have a 90 second timeout and no retry, and any error here is thrown up to the router.
debug: Check the router error log for the request. If every answer is a fallback, read the reason text, which says whether the draft or the check failed. If the no-facts message appears, confirm the run's facts are marked admitted. Model choice comes from the role settings in modelConfig.
